cond_0001.intro:
The Family & Child Development Lab at [Company name masked], directed by Dr. Ashley Groh, is recruiting a full-time research assistant. The research assistant will work on an NSF funded study on the human maternal brain over the transition to motherhood. Specifically, this study examines the interplay of maternal psychological risk (e.g., attachment insecurity, depression) and neural reactivity to infant cues (using EEG/ERP) on maternal and infant health and well-being across the perinatal period. The research assistant will be responsible for study management and behavioral and EEG data collection, reduction, and analysis.
The postgraduate associate will also support other tasks related to the team's research, such as manuscript preparation, grant writing, presentations at conferences, design of future studies, and other duties as assigned. This is an ideal position for someone looking to gain more research experience on topics related to parent-child relationships, neural processes (EEG/ERP), and development before pursuing a PhD in a related field (e.g., development psychology, neuroscience, clinical psychology, HDFS).
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Assist with all aspects of the research process: recruit and schedule participants; conduct lab visits with (expectant) mothers and infants; create and program stimuli; write protocols; assist with grant reports, manuscript preparations, and conference presentations
Assist with EEG/ERP and Observational Data Collection/Reduction: collect EEG/ERP and observational data from (expectant) mothers and infants; code, process, and analyze EEG/ERP and observational data
Assist with daily lab operations: purchase lab supplies and equipment; manage budgets, IRB protocols, participant database, website, social media, newsletters; establish and coordinate recruitment events (e.g. Baby Expos, Hospital Education Classes)
Lead a team of undergraduate research assistants: recruit and interview undergraduate research assistants; develop training manuals and provide training; assign daily and long-term tasks; supervise research assistant progress
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired
1-2 Years of research experience, preferably with infants and parents and with EEG/ERP methods
Experience working with parents and infants/children
Experience with EEG/ERP
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Exceptional project management and organizational skills, including good attention to detail
The ability to work both independently and in a collaborative environment
Exceptional time management and leadership skills
Self-motivated to learn new skills and solve problems independently, attentive to detail, and comfortable juggling multiple tasks
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with observational research methodologies and statistical analysis
Proficiency (or willingness to learn) R, SPSS, Qualtrics, Photoshop; expertise with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel)
Creativity and/or a design background (to help with stimuli creation, recruitment, newsletters)
Computer programming or web development skills
cond_0001.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

The Family & Child Development Lab at [Company name masked], directed by Dr. Ashley Groh, is recruiting a full-time research assistant. The research assistant will work on an NSF funded study on the human maternal brain over the transition to motherhood. Specifically, this study examines the interplay of maternal psychological risk (e.g., attachment insecurity, depression) and neural reactivity to infant cues (using EEG/ERP) on maternal and infant health and well-being across the perinatal period. The research assistant will be responsible for study management and behavioral and EEG data collection, reduction, and analysis.
The postgraduate associate will also support other tasks related to the team's research, such as manuscript preparation, grant writing, presentations at conferences, design of future studies, and other duties as assigned. This is an ideal position for someone looking to gain more research experience on topics related to parent-child relationships, neural processes (EEG/ERP), and development before pursuing a PhD in a related field (e.g., development psychology, neuroscience, clinical psychology, HDFS).
cond_0055.responsibilities:

Assist with EEG/ERP and Observational Data Collection/Reduction: collect EEG/ERP and observational data from (expectant) mothers and infants; code, process, and analyze EEG/ERP and observational data
Assist with daily lab operations: purchase lab supplies and equipment; manage budgets, IRB protocols, participant database, website, social media, newsletters; establish and coordinate recruitment events (e.g. Baby Expos, Hospital Education Classes)
Lead a team of undergraduate research assistants: recruit and interview undergraduate research assistants; develop training manuals and provide training; assign daily and long-term tasks; supervise research assistant progress
cond_0055.requirements:

High school diploma or equivalent and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired

Experience working with parents and infants/children
Experience with EEG/ERP
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

The ability to work both independently and in a collaborative environment
Exceptional time management and leadership skills
Self-motivated to learn new skills and solve problems independently, attentive to detail, and comfortable juggling multiple tasks
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with observational research methodologies and statistical analysis

This study examines the interplay of maternal psychological risk (e.g., attachment insecurity, depression) and neural reactivity to infant cues (using EEG/ERP) on maternal and infant health and well-being across the perinatal period. The research assistant will be responsible for study management and behavioral and EEG data collection, reduction, and analysis.
The postgraduate associate will also support other tasks related to the team's research, such as manuscript preparation, grant writing, conference presentations, design of future studies, and other duties as assigned. This is a good position for someone looking to gain more research experience on topics related to parent-child relationships, neural processes (EEG/ERP), and development before pursuing a PhD in a related field (e.g., developmental psychology, neuroscience, clinical psychology, HDFS).
cond_0115.responsibilities:
Assist with all aspects of the research process: recruit and schedule participants; conduct lab visits with (expectant) mothers and infants; create and program stimuli; write protocols; contribute to grant reports, manuscript preparations, and conference presentations
Assist with EEG/ERP and Observational Data Collection/Reduction: collect EEG/ERP and observational data from (expectant) mothers and infants; code, process, and analyze EEG/ERP and observational data
Assist with lab operations: purchase lab supplies and equipment; manage budgets, IRB protocols, participant database, website, social media, newsletters; coordinate recruitment events (e.g. Baby Expos, Hospital Education Classes)
Oversee a team of undergraduate research assistants: recruit and interview candidates; develop training manuals and deliver training; assign tasks; monitor research assistant progress
cond_0115.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired
1-2 Years of research experience, preferably with infants and parents and EEG/ERP methods
Experience working with parents and infants/children
Experience with EEG/ERP
Strong written communication and clear, direct verbal reporting
Exceptional project management and organizational skills, including close attention to detail
Ability to work independently and coordinate with others on specific tasks
Self-directed in learning new skills and solving problems, comfortable managing multiple tasks
Preferred Requirements
Exceptional time management and team oversight skills
Familiarity with observational research methodologies and statistical analysis
Proficiency (or willingness to learn) in R, SPSS, Qualtrics, Photoshop; working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel)
Creativity or a design background (to help with stimuli creation, recruitment materials, newsletters)
Computer programming or web development skills

The research assistant will collaborate on an NSF funded study on the human maternal brain over the transition to motherhood. Specifically, this study examines the interplay of maternal psychological risk (e.g., attachment insecurity, depression) and neural reactivity to infant cues (using EEG/ERP) on maternal and infant health and well-being across the perinatal period. The research assistant will work with the team on study management and behavioral and EEG data collection, reduction, and analysis.
The postgraduate associate will also support other tasks related to the team's research, such as manuscript preparation, grant writing, presentations at conferences, design of future studies, and other duties as assigned. This is an ideal position for someone looking to gain more research experience on topics related to parent-child relationships, neural processes (EEG/ERP), and development before pursuing a PhD in a related field (e.g., development psychology, neuroscience, clinical psychology, HDFS).
cond_0153.responsibilities:
Coordinate all aspects of the research process: recruit and schedule participants; conduct lab visits with (expectant) mothers and infants; create and program stimuli; write protocols; assist with grant reports, manuscript preparations, and conference presentations
Collaborate on EEG/ERP and Observational Data Collection/Reduction: collect EEG/ERP and observational data from (expectant) mothers and infants; code, process, and analyze EEG/ERP and observational data
Support daily lab operations: purchase lab supplies and equipment; help manage budgets, IRB protocols, participant database, website, social media, newsletters; coordinate recruitment events (e.g. Baby Expos, Hospital Education Classes)
Work alongside and coordinate a team of undergraduate research assistants: recruit and interview undergraduate research assistants; develop training manuals and provide training; assign daily and long-term tasks; support research assistant progress
cond_0153.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired
Experience working with parents and infants/children
Experience with EEG/ERP
1-2 Years of research experience, preferably with infants and parents and EEG/ERP methods
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Exceptional project management and organizational skills, including good attention to detail
The ability to work both independently and in a collaborative environment
Preferred Requirements
Exceptional time management and leadership skills
Self-motivated to learn new skills and solve problems independently, attentive to detail, and comfortable juggling multiple tasks
Familiarity with observational research methodologies and statistical analysis
Proficiency (or willingness to learn) R, SPSS, Qualtrics, Photoshop; expertise with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel)
Creativity and/or a design background (to help with stimuli creation, recruitment, newsletters)
Computer programming or web development skills
cond_0153.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

cond_0173.intro:

The research assistant will work on an NSF funded study on the human maternal brain over the transition to motherhood. Specifically, this study examines the interplay of maternal psychological risk (e.g., attachment insecurity, depression) and neural reactivity to infant cues (using EEG/ERP) on maternal and infant health and well-being across the perinatal period. The research assistant will be responsible for study management and behavioral and EEG data collection, reduction, and analysis.
The postgraduate associate will also support other tasks related to the team's research, such as manuscript preparation, grant writing, presentations at conferences, design of future studies, and other duties as assigned. This is an ideal position for someone looking to gain more research experience on topics related to parent-child relationships, neural processes (EEG/ERP), and development before pursuing a PhD in a related field (e.g., development psychology, neuroscience, clinical psychology, HDFS). People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with EEG/ERP methods and developmental research.
cond_0194.responsibilities:
Assist with all aspects of the research process: recruit and schedule participants; conduct lab visits with (expectant) mothers and infants; create and program stimuli; write protocols; assist with grant reports, manuscript preparations, and conference presentations
Assist with EEG/ERP and Observational Data Collection/Reduction: collect EEG/ERP and observational data from (expectant) mothers and infants; code, process, and analyze EEG/ERP and observational data
Assist with daily lab operations: purchase lab supplies and equipment; manage budgets, IRB protocols, participant database, website, social media, newsletters; establish and coordinate recruitment events (e.g. Baby Expos, Hospital Education Classes)
Lead a team of undergraduate research assistants: recruit and interview undergraduate research assistants; develop training manuals and provide training; assign daily and long-term tasks; supervise research assistant progress
cond_0194.requirements:
Experience working with parents and infants/children
Experience with EEG/ERP
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Exceptional project management skills, including good attention to detail
The ability to work both independently and in a collaborative environment
High school diploma or equivalent and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary
1-2 Years of research experience, preferably infants and parents AND with EEG/ERP methods
Exceptional organizational, time management, and leadership skills
Strong writing, communication, and interpersonal skills
Self-motivated to learn new skills and solve problems independently, attentive to detail, and comfortable juggling multiple tasks
Familiarity with observational research methodologies and statistical analysis
Proficiency (or willingness to learn) R, SPSS, Qualtrics, Photoshop; expertise with Microsoft office (Word, Excel)
Creativity and/or a design background (to help with stimuli creation, recruitment, newsletters)
Computer programming, or web development skills would be a plus
cond_0194.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0194.values: We value creating work that has a meaningful and positive effect on others. We believe fairness, respect, and responsibility should guide how we operate.

The research assistant will collaborate on an NSF funded study on the human maternal brain over the transition to motherhood. Specifically, this study examines the interplay of maternal psychological risk (e.g., attachment insecurity, depression) and neural reactivity to infant cues (using EEG/ERP) on maternal and infant health and well-being across the perinatal period. The research assistant will share responsibility for study management and behavioral and EEG data collection, reduction, and analysis.
The postgraduate associate will also support other tasks related to the team's research, such as manuscript preparation, grant writing, presentations at conferences, design of future studies, and other duties as assigned. This is an ideal position for someone looking to gain more research experience on topics related to parent-child relationships, neural processes (EEG/ERP), and development before pursuing a PhD in a related field (e.g., development psychology, neuroscience, clinical psychology, HDFS).
cond_0252.responsibilities:
Coordinate all aspects of the research process: recruit and schedule participants; conduct lab visits with (expectant) mothers and infants; create and program stimuli; write protocols; assist with grant reports, manuscript preparations, and conference presentations
Work alongside the team on EEG/ERP and Observational Data Collection/Reduction: collect EEG/ERP and observational data from (expectant) mothers and infants; code, process, and analyze EEG/ERP and observational data
Support daily lab operations: purchase lab supplies and equipment; manage budgets, IRB protocols, participant database, website, social media, newsletters; establish and coordinate recruitment events (e.g. Baby Expos, Hospital Education Classes)
Oversee and support a team of undergraduate research assistants: recruit and interview undergraduate research assistants; develop training manuals and provide training; assign daily and long-term tasks; supervise research assistant progress
cond_0252.requirements:
Experience working with parents and infants/children
Experience with EEG/ERP
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Exceptional project management skills, including good attention to detail
The ability to work both independently and in a collaborative environment
High school diploma or equivalent and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary
1-2 Years of research experience, preferably infants and parents AND with EEG/ERP methods
Exceptional organizational, time management, and leadership skills
Strong writing, communication, and interpersonal skills
Self-motivated to learn new skills and solve problems independently, attentive to detail, and comfortable juggling multiple tasks
Familiarity with observational research methodologies and statistical analysis
Proficiency (or willingness to learn) R, SPSS, Qualtrics, Photoshop; expertise with Microsoft office (Word, Excel)
Creativity and/or a design background (to help with stimuli creation, recruitment, newsletters)
Computer programming, or web development skills would be a plus
cond_0252.values: We value excellence, achievement, and delivering outcomes we can stand behind. We aim to bring high standards and a results-focused mindset to our work.
cond_0252.inclusion: However you identify or whatever your path here, please apply if you see a position that makes your heart skip a beat. Come join us and help us build a global company where we're all proud to belong. Confidence can sometimes hold us back from applying for a job. cond_0310.intro:
The Family & Child Development Lab at [Company name masked], directed by Dr. Ashley Groh, is recruiting a full-time research assistant. The research assistant will work on an NSF funded study on the human maternal brain over the transition to motherhood. Specifically, this study examines the interplay of maternal psychological risk (e.g., attachment insecurity, depression) and neural reactivity to infant cues (using EEG/ERP) on maternal and infant health and well-being across the perinatal period. The research assistant will be responsible for study management and behavioral and EEG data collection, reduction, and analysis.
The postgraduate associate will also support other tasks related to the team's research, such as manuscript preparation, grant writing, presentations at conferences, design of future studies, and other duties as assigned. This is an ideal position for someone looking to gain more research experience on topics related to parent-child relationships, neural processes (EEG/ERP), and development before pursuing a PhD in a related field (e.g., developmental psychology, neuroscience, clinical psychology, HDFS). People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of EEG/ERP methods and developmental research.
cond_0310.responsibilities:
Assist with all aspects of the research process: recruit and schedule participants; conduct lab visits with (expectant) mothers and infants; create and program stimuli; write protocols; assist with grant reports, manuscript preparations, and conference presentations
Assist with EEG/ERP and Observational Data Collection/Reduction: collect EEG/ERP and observational data from (expectant) mothers and infants; code, process, and analyze EEG/ERP and observational data
Assist with daily lab operations: purchase lab supplies and equipment; manage budgets, IRB protocols, participant database, website, social media, newsletters; establish and coordinate recruitment events (e.g. Baby Expos, Hospital Education Classes)
Lead a team of undergraduate research assistants: recruit and interview undergraduate research assistants; develop training manuals and provide training; assign daily and long-term tasks; supervise research assistant progress

Experience with EEG/ERP

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Exceptional project management and organizational skills, including good attention to detail
The ability to work both independently and in a collaborative environment
Exceptional time management and leadership skills
Self-motivated to learn new skills and solve problems independently, attentive to detail, and comfortable juggling multiple tasks
Preferred Requirements
Familiarity with observational research methodologies and statistical analysis
Proficiency (or willingness to learn) R, SPSS, Qualtrics, Photoshop; expertise with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel)
Creativity and/or a design background (to help with stimuli creation, recruitment, newsletters)
Computer programming or web development skills

The research assistant will work on an NSF funded study on the human maternal brain over the transition to motherhood. Specifically, this study examines the interplay of maternal psychological risk (e.g., attachment insecurity, depression) and neural reactivity to infant cues (using EEG/ERP) on maternal and infant health and well-being across the perinatal period. The research assistant will be responsible for study management and behavioral and EEG data collection, reduction, and analysis.
The postgraduate associate will also support other tasks related to the team's research, such as manuscript preparation, grant writing, presentations at conferences, design of future studies, and other duties as assigned. This is a good position for someone looking to gain more research experience on topics related to parent-child relationships, neural processes (EEG/ERP), and development before pursuing a PhD in a related field (e.g., developmental psychology, neuroscience, clinical psychology, HDFS).
cond_0330.responsibilities:
Assist with all aspects of the research process: actively recruit and schedule participants; conduct lab visits with (expectant) mothers and infants; create and program stimuli; write protocols; contribute to grant reports, manuscript preparations, and conference presentations
Assist with EEG/ERP and Observational Data Collection/Reduction: collect EEG/ERP and observational data from (expectant) mothers and infants; code, process, and analyze EEG/ERP and observational data
Assist with daily lab operations: purchase lab supplies and equipment; manage budgets, IRB protocols, participant database, website, social media, newsletters; coordinate and lead recruitment events (e.g. Baby Expos, Hospital Education Classes)
Lead a team of undergraduate research assistants: recruit and interview undergraduate research assistants; develop training manuals and provide training; assign daily and long-term tasks; supervise research assistant progress
cond_0330.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
High school diploma or equivalent and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired
1-2 Years of research experience, preferably with infants and parents and EEG/ERP methods
Experience working with parents and infants/children
Experience with EEG/ERP
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with comfort engaging regularly with participants, team members, and collaborators
Exceptional project management and organizational skills, including close attention to detail
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively
Preferred Requirements
Exceptional time management and leadership skills
Familiarity with observational research methodologies and statistical analysis
Proficiency (or willingness to learn) R, SPSS, Qualtrics, Photoshop; working knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel)
Creativity and/or a design background (to help with stimuli creation, recruitment, newsletters)
Computer programming or web development skills
cond_0330.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

cond_0550.intro:
